title: batchAuthzSearcher warns when a search matches documents but authorizes none
answers: Why does a LIST return no items even though documents matched the search query?
How do I debug a permission check that silently filters out every search hit?
Where is 'search found candidates but 0 authorized' logged?
body:
Symptom: a LIST/search returns an empty page even though matching documents exist in the index, with no error — e.g. the authorizing token has no delegated permissions and every candidate gets denied.
Root cause: before this PR the only record of 'candidates found, none authorized' was a trace span attribute (search.candidates/search.authorized), invisible in log-only environments.
Fix pattern: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:batchAuthzSearcher.Close calls logIfNothingAuthorized, which emits a Warn log with namespace, group, resources, candidates and authorized counts whenever candidates>0 and authorized==0.
Constraints: known imprecision (accepted, not fixed): if FilterAuthorized hits a BatchCheck error mid-stream, candidates can be pulled without authorized being incremented, so this warning can also fire on an authz-backend error/cancellation, not just a true all-denied result — don't treat the log alone as proof of a permission gap, check for a concurrent BatchCheck error too.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/search batch authorization filtering of search results
says: Search returns nothing even though items match the query
List shows empty results while matching documents exist
Permissions silently filter out every result from a search
Why does the search hide documents it found but can't authorize
Authorization secretly removes all matching search results
search: Warning log emitted when a search finds candidate documents but zero results are authorized, preventing silent empty-result gaps. The pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:batchAuthzSearcher.Close method calls logIfNothingAuthorized to emit a Warn-level log with namespace, group, resources, and candidate/authorized counts whenever candidates > 0 and authorized == 0. Known imprecision: if FilterAuthorized encounters a BatchCheck error mid-stream, the warning can fire on authorization-backend failure rather than true all-denied, so don't treat the log alone as proof of a permission gap without checking for concurrent BatchCheck errors. Applies to pkg/storage/unified/search batch authorization filtering of search results.
